title: 00 — ML Engineering: Index
html:
00 — ML Engineering: Index

The one idea: a machine-learning model is a function fitted to past data, and almost everything that goes wrong comes from the data and the evaluation, not the algorithm. This set builds each core method from scratch, so you can see how it works, then shows how the same thing is done in production on Databricks.

1. What this set is

AI & ML Foundations gives the map of the field, and LLM Engineering & RAG covers building with language models. This set fills the space between them, from beginner to senior ML engineer:

  • Fundamentals, built by hand: logistic regression, gradient boosting, a neural network and attention, written in about 30 lines of numpy each, so nothing is a black box.
  • Evaluation done properly: splits, leakage, imbalanced metrics, calibration, walk-forward backtests.
  • Financial ML: credit scorecards and forecasting of flows and nowcasts.
  • Modern practice: feature stores and point-in-time joins, fine-tuning with LoRA, and MLOps on Databricks with MLflow, Unity Catalog and Model Serving.

Every runnable example uses only numpy and pandas with made-up data, and the output shown is the real output. Code that needs Databricks, scikit-learn, PyTorch or other packages is marked not run.

2. Chapter map

# Chapter Level What you get from it
01 Training and Evaluation from Scratch Beginner Logistic regression by gradient descent, splits, AUC, precision and recall, calibration, leakage
02 Features and Feature Stores Beginner to senior Feature engineering, point-in-time joins, training-serving skew, Databricks feature store
03 Trees, Boosting and Tuning Intermediate Decision trees, gradient boosting from scratch, XGBoost and LightGBM, Optuna
04 Time Series Forecasting and Nowcasting Intermediate Baselines, seasonality, walk-forward backtests, MASE, nowcasts
05 Credit Risk Modelling Intermediate to senior PD, WoE and IV, scorecards, Gini and KS, model risk governance
06 Neural Networks and Transformers from Scratch Intermediate Backpropagation, attention, embeddings, how an LLM is built
07 Fine-Tuning and LoRA Senior When to fine-tune, LoRA and QLoRA mechanics, evaluation, GPUs, Databricks options
08 MLOps on Databricks End to End Senior MLflow, the Unity Catalog registry and aliases, serving, inference tables, monitoring, retraining, CI/CD

3. Reading order

  1. Read AI & ML Foundations first for the vocabulary.
  2. Then 01 → 02 → 03 in order. They are the core of every tabular ML project.
  3. 04 and 05 apply the core to financial problems.
  4. 06 → 07 for deep learning and language models. Read LLM Engineering & RAG alongside them.
  5. 08 to run any of it in production.

The Learning Paths set places these chapters in a full beginner-to-senior plan, together with data engineering and Databricks.
